# Event fixtures

Contract fixtures of the **subscriber**: what `brain note` expects from an event. They are not generated by the
module that emits the event; they record the expectation of the consumer so that the emitting side can be checked
against them: `scripts/test-event-contracts.py` of the repository validates every `valid-*` fixture against the data
schema of the producer (`valid-additive*` against the envelope only), and a mismatch is fixed in the consumer.

## `planner.plan.closed/`

Envelope: `event/v1` (`specversion "1.0"`, `source "urn:swissknifeman:module:planner"`,
`type "planner.plan.closed"`). `data` is an object:

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan_id` | non-empty string | yes |
| `title` | non-empty string | yes |
| `short_id`, `status`, `goal`, `repository` | string | no |
| `closed_at` | RFC 3339 string (the event `time` is used when absent) | no |
| `phases` | array of `{id, title, status}` | no |
| `counts` | object of non-negative integers (`items`, `done`, `done_with_deviations`, `skipped`, `blocked`) | no |
| `artifacts` | array | no (not read) |

Unknown fields are ignored on every level (additive evolution).

| File | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| `valid-minimal.json` | note written (the required fields only: `plan_id`, `title`, and `status` which the producer always sets) |
| `valid-full.json` | note written (every known field) |
| `valid-additive.json` | note written, extra fields ignored, `closed_at` with an offset |
| `other-type.json` | skipped (`EVENT_TYPE_IGNORED`) |
| `invalid-no-plan-id.json` | refused (`EVENT_DATA_INVALID`, exit 65) |
| `invalid-data-not-object.json` | refused (`EVENT_DATA_INVALID`, exit 65) |
| `invalid-specversion.json` | refused (`EVENT_DATA_INVALID`, exit 65) |

The tests in `tests/test_events.py` check every file. Add a fixture when the expectation changes; never edit one to
make a test pass.
